subject: Regulatory addenda feasibility: SummitTrust pilot & cross-entity data flows
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@summittrust.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Reg addenda feasibility: SummitTrust pilot & cross-entity data flows

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick follow-up and outline so we can align the legal/procurement asks before the pilot kickoff:

Summary of what we understood on the call:
- Pilot scope: inference for transaction-scoring model (tokenized account metadata + hashed PII) for SummitTrust fraud team.
- Primary regulatory surface: GLBA (financial services). There may be a downstream reporting feed to a benefits partner that handles PHI, so HIPAA/BAA could be relevant if PHI flows to that partner.
- Residency ask: SummitTrust wants US-only residency for customer data and no subprocessor processing in jurisdictions outside North America.
- Timeline: procurement aiming to complete contracting by end of Q2 (we discussed a target of ~90 days).

Immediate items we can provide:
1) Redwood draft DPA (attached) + a short GLBA addendum scope doc to propose the minimal language needed for your counsel to review.
2) Current subprocessor inventory and SOC2 Type II summary (we can share SOC2 report under NDA/portal link).
3) Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owner assignments.

Ask for you: can you confirm whether SummitTrust requires an explicit BAA for the benefits partner path or if they prefer to handle that with their vendor? Also confirm whether a limited residency guarantee (US-only for production data, analytics allowed in EU for anonymized telemetry) is acceptable or if they require a hard technical block.

I attached: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf and GLBA_Addendum_Scope.docx.

Proposed next step: Laura (cc'd) and I can put together a one-page MAP and a redline of the addendum for your counsel. If procurement wants a single consolidated contract flow (SOW + DPA + addenda) we can accommodate.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (12 KB summary stub)
From: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@summittrust.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@summittrust.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Reg addenda feasibility: SummitTrust pilot & cross-entity data flows

Diego —

Thanks for the concise summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Procurement will need the full subprocessor list (names + country of operations) and an explanation of which subprocessors handle raw tokens vs telemetry/observability.
- Our security team flagged the potential HIPAA surface because the benefits partner ingests claims-level information that could be tied back to identifiers. For now, our preference is that Redwood propose BAA language we can review; if the partner is the one ingesting PHI, we may ask Redwood to support contractual language that limits processing to the extent necessary.
- Residency: SummitTrust's data residency policy requires production customer data to remain within US-controlled infrastructure. We are open to allowing aggregated telemetry to be processed outside the US as long as it's not linkable to customer IDs.

Procurement timeline: we typically have a 6–8 week procurement window once we have a clean set of documents (DPA + addendum + SOW). If legal flags substantive redlines, that can extend.

Please send the subprocessor list and SOC2 artefacts (we can receive SOC2 via secure portal). Also please indicate if Redwood supports a dedicated (tenant-isolated) deployment for SummitTrust as an option for stricter isolation.

Thanks,
Susan
Director, Vendor Risk Management
SummitTrust Credit Cooperative
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@summittrust.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 10:25:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Reg addenda feasibility: SummitTrust pilot & cross-entity data flows

Susan —

Appreciate the clarity. Looping in Mina (Legal) and Laura (Customer Success) to propose a concrete path forward. Quick answers inline + proposed MAP: 

- Subprocessors: attached is the current list (summary in the GLBA scope doc). We separate subprocessors that touch customer payloads (inference engine, KV cache) from those that handle observability/telemetry. We will prepare an export that tags each subprocessor by service and country.
- SOC2: we can share the full report via secure portal — link will follow from our compliance team.
- Dedicated option: Redwood can support a dedicated capacity pool (redwood dedicated) which provides GPU/tier isolation and optionally VPC peering for stricter network controls. That would be a separate procurement line item; estimate + lead times in the MAP.

Proposed MAP (high level) — target 8 weeks to contract signature if SummitTrust proceeds now:
1) Week 0: Exchange DPA + GLBA addendum scope (attached) — (Owner: Redwood / Diego)
2) Week 1: Redwood submits full subprocessor inventory + SOC2 portal link — (Owner: Redwood / Mina)
3) Week 2–3: SummitTrust legal redlines DPA/addendum; security completes tech review — (Owner: SummitTrust)
4) Week 3–5: Negotiation/redlines; decide on dedicated capacity if required — (Owners: Redwood + SummitTrust Procurement)
5) Week 6–8: Finalize signatures, SOW, onboarding dates — (Owners: both)

I've attached the GLBA_Addendum_Scope.docx and included the SOC2 summary. Mina — can you provide quick guidance on our negotiation posture for GLBA/BAA language and any redline suggestions we should pre-surface?

Next steps: Mina and Laura will prepare the redline and the MAP (1 page) and we will send the SOC2 portal link by EOD Monday.

Best,
Diego
Attachment: GLBA_Addendum_Scope.docx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@summittrust.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Reg addenda feasibility: SummitTrust pilot & cross-entity data flows

Susan / team —

Thanks for the context — adding legal perspective and a suggested approach. High level: Redwood is comfortable with a limited GLBA addendum that references the base DPA and adds targeted clauses around (1) customer data residency, (2) subprocessor restrictions, and (3) permitted processing for fraud detection. For any HIPAA/BAA exposure tied to the benefits partner, we propose to: 1) include a conditional BAA-ready clause (we will accept an executed BAA where required) or 2) scope the DPA to exclude PHI unless explicitly agreed and routed via a BAA workflow.

Suggested redlines to pre-surface (summary):
- Residency: Insert a residency SLA that production customer data shall be stored and processed only in data centers located in the United States, with exceptions for de-identified telemetry defined by a strict de-identification standard.
- Subprocessors: Acceptable to provide subprocessor list + 30-day notice for new subprocessors, carve out an audit right for critical subprocessors, and agree to contract flow-downs for those that process customer payloads.
- GLBA-specific: Add a clause that Redwood will assist in incident response and provide audit support for regulatory exams; preserve indemnity limitations but offer targeted cooperation commitments.
- HIPAA/BAA: We can accept a conditional BAA path — Redwood will sign a BAA if PHI flows to Redwood-managed systems; if PHI flows directly to SummitTrust's partner, Redwood will provide data flow mapping and support partner-level BAAs but will not be the PHI holder in those cases.

I'll attach a short redline (annotated DPA) and a one-page MAP that calls out milestones and timing. If SummitTrust prefers hard technical enforcement (no non-US processing), let's surface that as an SOW/dedicated deployment ask — we will provide cost and lead-time impacts in the MAP.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (annotated), GLBA_Addendum_Scope.docx (annotated), SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (portal reference available).

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
